data.title: OpenAI confirms it’s working with Anthropic, Google to address AI risks
data.description:
OpenAI is working with rivals Anthropic and Google DeepMind on steps to address AI safety, as industry and lawmakers respond to growing concern that the technology poses economic and security risks.

Chris Lehane, OpenAI’s global policy chief, said Tuesday the engagement had been under way for several weeks.

He added that OpenAI does not believe the three companies need an antitrust waiver to coordinate on safety matters.

“It’s better to try to work together to prioritize safety,” Lehane said at a briefing in Washington, as per a Bloomberg report.

Amodei’s essay sparked wider attention

Concern over AI’s risks moved into the mainstream after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei published a 3,800-word essay on Saturday, calling for restraint in developing the most advanced AI systems so researchers can better understand potential threats.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and SpaceX and xAI chief Elon Musk both publicly backed the essay’s message.

But according to The Information, talks between the three companies on a shared industry standards body had already been under way since at least July, with working-group meetings held as recently as last week.

The original push came from a July essay by Google DeepMind founder Demis Hassabis, who proposed a standards body modeled on the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority, which oversees Wall Street under SEC supervision.

Hassabis envisioned an organization that would evaluate advanced AI models before release, funded by industry but staffed with independent technical experts.

Lawmakers divided, Trump dismissive

Lehane said he was in Washington meeting lawmakers and that OpenAI would support bipartisan proposals to address catastrophic AI risks.

The measures include a federal AI governance framework proposed by Republican Representative Jay Obernolte and Democrat Lori Trahan, as well as a Senate proposal led by Majority Leader John Thune, Republican Ted Cruz and Democrat Amy Klobuchar.

A separate bill from Senators Jim Banks and Adam Schiff would give AI companies a limited antitrust exemption to share information about risks, including loss of control over AI systems, cyber threats and Chinese attempts to exfiltrate data.

That measure has been folded into the annual defense bill.

Still, the odds of any AI legislation passing this year are low.

The House leaves Washington Thursday and won’t return until after the November elections, and the brief lame-duck session afterward is expected to focus on the Pentagon budget instead.

President Trump has publicly opposed AI safety guardrails, dismissing concerns raised by Anthropic and OpenAI as “a hoax” in social media posts Monday.

Industry itself is split

Not all AI companies support the coordination effort.

Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg raised concerns about a national AI regulator in an August call with Trump, according to The Information, and a related White House draft executive order was shelved after failing to gain sufficient backing within the administration.

House Speaker Mike Johnson told CNN on Sunday there is “no consensus” among the AI companies on what standards should look like, adding that any framework would need to be a partnership between industry and lawmakers.

Cohere CEO Aidan Gomez was more pointed in his criticism, warning on X that letting the largest AI companies set shared rules could disadvantage smaller competitors.

data.title: Why is Cardano price falling despite the x402 integration?
data.description:
ADA has fallen roughly 3% over the past 24 hours to trade near $0.204 on Sept. 15, extending its seven-day loss despite Cardano’s recent integration with the x402 payment standard.

CoinGecko puts ADA at roughly $0.204, down more than 7% over the past week, after the token traded above $0.22 on Sept. 9 and briefly recovered towards $0.214 earlier on Monday. 

The latest rebound was quickly sold, leaving the token just above the $0.20 level.

Cardano’s x402 integration has failed to reverse the decline so far. 

The payment standard uses the HTTP 402 protocol to let software, including autonomous AI agents, make machine-to-machine payments without conventional accounts or checkout systems, giving Cardano developers another way to build automated payment applications.

The integration, however, does not require users or developers to immediately buy large amounts of ADA. 

Its effect on the token would depend on applications adopting x402 on Cardano, transaction activity increasing, and ADA capturing demand generated by those applications.

Price action over the past week shows that buying has remained weak despite the announcement. 

ADA started the period above $0.22, fell towards $0.205 by Sept. 11 and spent much of the following sessions struggling below $0.21. 

Monday’s rebound towards $0.214 was rejected before the token returned to roughly $0.204.

The decline extends a pattern that has developed since late August. 

ADA traded above $0.24 and briefly moved considerably higher around Aug. 22, but sellers pushed it back towards $0.20. 

Another recovery in early September stalled around $0.23, leaving successive rebounds below the August peak.

Pressure across the crypto market has made those recoveries harder to sustain. 

Bitcoin has slipped below the $77,000-$77,500 region while traders face uncertainty around the Federal Reserve’s policy decision and the US Senate’s CLARITY Act proceedings.

US Treasury yields have climbed as oil prices above $100 renewed inflation concerns, creating a difficult backdrop for risk assets.

ADA’s recent derivatives positioning has created another source of pressure. 

Long-heavy positioning leaves leveraged traders exposed when the spot price falls, as liquidations can force positions to close during a decline and increase short-term selling.

ADA price analysis

ADA’s daily chart keeps the larger downtrend intact despite its recovery from the June low near $0.145. 

Price climbed as high as roughly $0.245 in August but failed to regain the large volume area around $0.245-$0.25, where the Volume Profile shows one of the strongest concentrations of historical trading activity.

The Volume Profile places another large trading cluster around $0.17-$0.18. With ADA now near $0.204, price is sitting between those two major volume zones. 

A break below $0.20 would leave the $0.18 area as the first notable downside target, followed by the high-volume region around $0.17. 

Losing that area could expose the June zone near $0.145-$0.15.

Aroon readings on the daily chart favour sellers. Aroon Down stands near 50%, while Aroon Up has dropped to roughly 7.1%. 

The low Aroon Up reading shows that ADA has not made a recent high strong enough to establish an active upward trend. 

A move back above $0.22 would begin to change the recent price structure, while the larger resistance zone remains around $0.24-$0.25.

On the 4-hour chart, ADA is trading near $0.2046 and remains below the Supertrend resistance at roughly $0.2167. See below.

Price briefly pushed above $0.21 during the latest rebound but could not hold the move, keeping the Supertrend bearish. 

ADA would need to reclaim $0.2167 and then clear the recent $0.22-$0.23 highs before $0.24-$0.25 comes back into range.

Chaikin Money Flow has fallen to roughly -0.21 on the 4-hour chart, moving further below zero as ADA returned towards $0.20. 

The negative reading shows that selling pressure has outweighed buying pressure across the indicator’s lookback period. 

A recovery above zero alongside a move through $0.2167 would provide stronger confirmation that buyers are returning.

For the downside, $0.20 remains the immediate level to watch. A clean break below it would expose roughly $0.19 before the $0.17-$0.18 volume cluster. 

Holding $0.20 and reclaiming the 4-hour Supertrend near $0.2167 would instead put $0.23 in view, followed by the much stronger $0.24-$0.25 resistance area.

data.title: Coinbase stock on edge as CLARITY Act odds of passing dip despite Trump concessions
data.description:
Coinbase stock jumped by nearly 10% on Monday after President Donald Trump made a major concession on the CLARITY Act and as Bitcoin and other tokens held steady. COIN jumped to $191.50, up by over 37% from its lowest level this year. 

Coinbase stock jumps after CLARITY Act concession

COIN stock jumped by nearly 10% on Monday after President Trump made some major concessions on the CLARITY Act. The new agreement allows for state attorneys general to take enforcement action on violations of the law, not just the Justice Department.

Another key concession is that the bill would require government officials to divest any significant financial interest in an entity that issues cryptocurrencies. This provision became of significant importance after Trump reported that he made over $2 billion last year from his crypto holdings. 

Trump is a major player in the crypto industry. He launched the TRUMP meme coin last year, with thousands of people losing a fortune as its price plunged. Trump also launched World Liberty Financial, which operates the USD1 stablecoin. World Liberty recently received a provisional bank charter from the OCC. 

Trump Media is also a big holder of Bitcoin, while his sons have large stakes in companies in the crypto industry, including American Bitcoin. 

The CLARITY Act would benefit a company like Coinbase because of its strong presence across various industries. It is the biggest exchange in the United States. It is also a top custodian of crypto ETFs and a major player in the stablecoin industry through its partnership with Circle. 

The act will transfer most of the regulatory authority from the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) to the smaller Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC). Coinbase has been at odds with the SEC in the past. 

Still, despite the recent concessions by Trump, traders on Polymarket believe that the bill will not become law this year. Odds of the bill being passed have dropped to 19% from the year-to-date high from nearly 80%. 

Coinbase’s business is on a transition

COIN stock remains in a tight range as the company remains in a transition from being merely a crypto company into a platform to trade all assets. It has already used real-world asset (RWA) tokenization technology to offer stocks, commodities, and ETFs. 

The company has also become an important player in the predictions market through a partnership with Kalshi. These initiatives aim at helping the company offset the seasonality of the crypto industry. 

This transition explains why analysts have started upgrading the company. Compass Point hiked the rating from sell to neutral, with the target from $130 to $177. Morgan Stanley initiated the stock with a target of $250, while Goldman Sachs hiked its rating from $196 to $219. 

Coinbase stock is also benefiting from the resilience of the crypto market. Bitcoin remains above $78,000, while the crypto market cap jumped to over $2.6 trillion.

Coinbase stock technical analysis

COIN stock chart | Source: TradingView

Technicals suggest that the COIN stock has more upside to go. It has formed a bullish flag pattern, which normally leads to more upside over time. 

The stock has moved above the 50-day Exponential Moving Average (EMA). It is also slightly above $181, its highest level on July 21. Therefore, these technicals point to more gains, which will be confirmed if it moves above the key resistance at $193, the upper side of the horizontal channel.

data.title: Meta stock outlook: can Muse AI and legal relief push shares above $700?
data.description:
Meta Platforms’ stock META has been caught between enthusiasm over its artificial intelligence ambitions and concerns about the enormous cost of funding those efforts.

The latest rebound is giving bulls fresh reason to believe the company could finally be approaching a sustained breakout, Bloomberg reported, although analysts remain divided over whether the rally can last.

Meta shares have risen 22% from their August low and are on track for their strongest monthly gain since May 2025.

The recovery accelerated after the company settled a major social-media lawsuit and introduced Muse, an AI agent designed to automate everyday tasks for consumers.

The developments have helped revive the investment case for Meta after a year of repeated rallies that ultimately failed to hold.

Meta stock has already experienced four trough-to-peak gains of at least 20% in 2026.

Each rally subsequently faded, with the stock recording lower highs along the way.

That has left the shares essentially flat for the year, compared with a roughly 15% gain for the Nasdaq 100.

Meta was up about 1.4% today, touching $675.

Bulls see catalysts for a breakout

Investors betting on a sustained recovery believe the latest combination of legal relief and AI product momentum could be different.

"Eliminating a legal overhang and then having a positive product in a hot narrative is certainly enough to get the early stages of a trend change going," Dan Russo, co-chief investment officer at Potomac Fund Management, which owns Meta shares, said in the Bloomberg report.

"We've seen a number of these counter-trend rallies fizzle out and fade. What's key from here is to build on the momentum and validate the changing trend."

For Russo, that validation would require Meta stock to break decisively above $700 and remain there.

The $18 billion settlement of Meta's social-media lawsuit has also removed a significant source of uncertainty.

The company had previously calculated that an adverse trial outcome could have exposed it to penalties of as much as $1.4 trillion.

Meta shares have fallen in only four of the 12 trading sessions since the settlement was announced on Aug. 26.

AI products strengthen the investment case

The legal resolution has arrived alongside renewed optimism about Meta’s AI ambitions.

Morgan Stanley analyst Brian Nowak compared Meta’s current setup with Alphabet’s position in late 2025, when the Google parent received a favourable ruling in a long-running antitrust case and subsequently launched a series of AI products.

Alphabet shares have since gained more than 50%, becoming the best-performing Magnificent Seven stock over that period.

Nowak believes Meta could similarly benefit as it continues to roll out AI products.

Meta is in position to keep releasing new products, "which in aggregate could add $10+ to EPS," Nowak wrote in an Aug. 30 note.

"We don't believe these are priced in Meta right now," he added, arguing that the stock is trading below its valuation peak in 2025, when investors viewed Meta as an "AI winner" and GPU investments were helping drive faster growth.

JPMorgan has also become more positive, upgrading Meta to overweight last week.

Analyst Doug Anmuth cited "strong early traction" for Muse and said the product demonstrated why Meta could have an advantage in bringing consumer-focused AI products to its enormous user base.

"Meta is well-positioned to deliver consumer-driven AI products to its base of about 4B users," Anmuth said.

"There's still meaningful upside potential as Meta is in the early stages of releasing frontier models and AI-driven products beyond advertising," he added.

Cheap valuation comes with a big spending risk

Meta’s valuation could provide another reason for investors to consider the stock after its recent weakness.

The company trades at roughly 18 times estimated earnings for the next 12 months, below its 10-year average of about 20 times and more than 30% below its 2025 peak.

At the same time, analysts expect revenue to grow by more than 25% this year, while earnings are forecast to increase by more than 30%.

But the stock’s relatively inexpensive valuation also reflects concerns about the enormous investment required to compete in AI.

Meta's capital expenditure is expected to nearly double to about $140 billion this year and rise to almost $200 billion in 2027.

That spending is expected to put substantial pressure on free cash flow.

After previously generating significant cash flows, Meta is projected to post negative free cash flow of about $6.3 billion this year, with the deficit potentially widening to almost $30 billion in 2027.

Investors remain divided over the rally

Those spending requirements are keeping some investors from fully embracing Meta’s recovery.

Cyrus Amini, chief investment officer at Hyphen Wealth Management, said the stock’s valuation and near-term catalysts were attractive, but questioned whether those factors were enough to support a longer-term rally.

"The valuation is attractive, and it could have more short-term catalysts than megacaps, but for anything beyond that, all bets are off. It could easily fade again," he said in the Bloomberg report.

"Things are changing so fast it's hard to safely say any name is a long-term winner."

data.title: Why Joby Aviation stock is falling as it nears a major inflection point
data.description:
Joby Aviation stock remains in a freefall this week and is hovering at its lowest level since May 2025. It slipped to $6.30, down more than 70% from its high last year, with its valuation falling from over $17.4 billion to $6.2 billion today. This retreat may continue, even as the company’s commercialization nears. 

Joby Aviation is at an inflection point

Joby Aviation is one of the top companies that seeks to disrupt the transportation industry. It has spent the last 17 years working on its electric vertical takeoff and landing aircraft (eVTOL). 

In this period, it has spent billions of dollars researching and working on its flights. To achieve that, it has received substantial funding from companies like Baillie Gifford and Toyota. Toyota has now become a crucial shareholder with a 14.3% stake. 

The company has also raised capital through dilution. It has raised cash by selling shares in the past few years. As a result, the outstanding shares have jumped from 604 million in 2022 to 986 million today. 

Most importantly, Joby has used this period to seek FAA certification, which it will receive later this year. The company has also expanded its manufacturing process and is using Toyota’s track record in the industry. It has also made some notable customer deals, including with ANA and Virgin Atlantic.

At the same time, it is now expanding its presence in the defense industry. It is doing that by spending $500 million to acquire Resonant Sciences, which will now become its defense business. 

Resonant made over $100 million in revenue in the trailing twelve months and is growing by 40%. This matters because the US government plans to spend over $1.5 trillion on defense. 

READ MORE: Here’s why flying car stocks like Joby and Archer Aviation falling

The company plans to start its commercial events this year, and then scale it in the foreseeable future. Taken together, its commercialization and the ongoing pivot towards the defense industry mean that it is at an inflection point.

Analysts expect that its revenue, excluding Resonant, will continue growing, with its annual revenue rising to $125 million this year and $299 million next year.

Concerns about its business remains

Joby Aviation stock has slipped in the past few months as investors remain concerned about its business. This explains why it has a short interest of about 10%, a sign that investors expect it to continue its downward trend. 

One of the key concerns is that it will take a long time for the company to become profitable even when the commercialization process starts. This will see it continue raising capital, possibly through share sales. It recently announced a $750 million share sale to finance its Resonant business.

Joby Aviation stock technical analysis

JOBY Aviation chart | Source: TradingView

The weekly chart shows that the JOBY share price has slumped in the past few years, falling from a record high of $21 to the current $6.30. It has formed a descending channel, a sign that bears remain in control.

The stock has dropped below the 78.6% Fibonacci Retracement level. It also fell below the 50-week and 100-week Exponential Moving Averages (EMA). Also, the Average Directional Index (ADX) has risen to 17.30 and is pointing upwards. 

Therefore, the stock will likely continue falling, potentially to the key support level of $4.87, its lowest level in October 2024 and April last year.

data.title: Why is Alphabet (GOOG) stock falling today?
data.description:
Alphabet shares GOOGL fell about 1.7% on Tuesday as higher crude prices, elevated Treasury yields and renewed uncertainty over AI demand weighed on technology stocks.

The decline came as investors prepared for what is widely expected to be another Federal Reserve interest-rate increase.

Traders were pricing in a nearly 93% probability of a hike on Wednesday, while the benchmark 10-year US Treasury yield climbed to its highest level since 2007.

Other major technology stocks also came under pressure.

Amazon fell about 1.7%, while Microsoft declined roughly 1%.

The Roundhill Magnificent Seven ETF was down 0.8%.

The weakness came despite a recovery in semiconductor stocks following Monday's sharp selloff, suggesting investors remain selective about which parts of the AI trade they are willing to back.

Higher yields raise pressure on AI spending

The rise in Treasury yields is particularly important for technology companies because much of their valuation is based on earnings and revenue expected several years into the future.

Higher borrowing costs can make those future cash flows less valuable while increasing the cost of financing the enormous infrastructure investments required to develop and deploy AI.

The issue has become more pressing as major technology companies increasingly turn to debt markets to finance their AI build-outs.

Alphabet was reported last month to be seeking between $20 billion and $25 billion through a US bond offering, following a sharp selloff triggered by concerns around its 2026 capital spending outlook.

A regulatory filing showed that the company offered notes in as many as 10 parts, with maturities ranging from two to 40 years.

Alphabet is not alone in tapping debt markets.

Amazon, Alphabet, Meta and Oracle issued about $194 billion worth of bonds through July 7, up 79% from roughly $108 billion during the same period in 2025, according to a Reuters analysis of LSEG data.

At the same time, the hyperscalers are expected to spend more than $730 billion this year, primarily on AI.

The scale of that investment is already putting pressure on cash generation.

Alphabet reported its first-ever negative free cash flow in the second quarter in late July.

AI slowdown fears add another layer of uncertainty

Investors are also reassessing whether the extraordinary pace of AI investment can continue as industry leaders raise concerns about the technology's risks.

AI-linked stocks suffered a global selloff on Monday after leaders of major AI companies warned about potentially existential risks associated with the technology.

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called on AI companies to slow the pace of model development in an essay posted on X on Saturday. Elon Musk and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman subsequently expressed agreement with Amodei.

Altman also said OpenAI would not proceed with an IPO this year, citing safety concerns.

The comments have raised questions about whether a slower pace of AI development could eventually translate into weaker infrastructure demand and lower capital spending.

However, some analysts see little evidence of an immediate slowdown.

Bank of America analyst Vivek Arya wrote in a Tuesday note that despite concerns over AI investment, "we see no signs of slowing in customer orders, [long-term agreements], capacity commitments or semis pricing."

That suggests the fundamental demand behind the AI infrastructure buildout remains intact, even as investors become increasingly sensitive to the amount companies are spending to meet it.

Fundstrat sees Magnificent Seven breakout

Despite the near-term pressure on Big Tech, some technical analysts remain optimistic about the sector's prospects.

Fundstrat believes the Magnificent Seven basket of mega-cap technology stocks is approaching a breakout that could trigger a broader rally in large-cap technology, MarketWatch reported.

"MAGS is on the verge of breaking out and looks quite positive here, with stocks like Apple, Alphabet, and Meta having all firmed up nicely in recent days," said Fundstrat's Newton.

"These look more appealing than many semiconductor names, many of which have stabilized but whose rally has proven to be a work in progress - not dissimilar to what happened to software earlier this year," he added.

According to Newton, the ETF is close to moving above the 70.80 level reached on Sept. 3.

A break above that level could trigger a sharp rally in the Nasdaq 100 and large-cap technology stocks over the following weeks.

"While Nvidia and Amazon have both weakened ever so slightly in recent days, neither has shown sufficient technical deterioration to think these cannot rally back as the Magnificent [Seven] ETF breaks out - which I see as being imminent," he concluded.

For Alphabet, the competing forces leave investors balancing two very different narratives.

Rising yields and massive AI spending are creating concerns about financing costs and cash flow, while continued customer demand and the possibility of a Magnificent Seven breakout are keeping the bullish case alive.

The post Why is Alphabet (GOOG) stock falling today? appeared first on Invezz

data.title: Dan Niles admits 10-year could hit 6%: stay bullish on Meta stock
data.description:
Niles Investment Management founder Dan Niles says investors should prepare for stickier, higher interest rates, noting that the 10-year Treasury yield could realistically climb to as much as 6%.

Pointing to unprecedented peacetime deficit spending, huge national debt expansion, and intense corporate debt issuance from tech giants competing against the US government, Niles believes rate pressures are far from over.

Despite anticipating a 10% correction leading into the upcoming midterms, however, he remains strongly conviction-long on Meta Platforms (META), citing unlocked AI monetization channels and an attractive valuation relative to broader technology peers.

How Niles recommends playing US stocks

Facing a potential surge in 10-year yields, Dan Niles emphasizes three primary tactical rules: avoid fighting the Federal Reserve, do not fight the bond market, and respect what he called the historical market seasonality.

With the federal deficit hovering around 6% of GDP and national debt standing against the gross domestic product, structural pressures prevent monetary authorities from artificially suppressing long-term rates as aggressively as in previous cycles.

Plus, seasonal drawdown trends surrounding midterm elections historically drag stocks down by 10% between late July and early November – double the pullbacks seen in non-midterm years.

With the market continually pitching risky volatility against elevated valuations, Niles advised disciplined investors in a CNBC interview that they are under no obligation to swing at every pitch.

Why Niles is still bullish on META stock

While holding significant short positions across the broader market, Niles maintains an outright bullish stance on Meta Platforms.

Unlike mega-cap peers like Microsoft, Amazon, or Google, META previously faced skepticism regarding its ability to monetize massive AI capex without a traditional cloud infrastructure or API platform.

However, recent breakthroughs – including cost-effective open model deployments, expanded enterprise API integrations, and new AI agent rollouts across its 3.6 billion daily active users – have fundamentally altered that narrative.

Trading at about 17x projected earnings, Meta stock presents a valuation lower than the broader S&P 500 index and significantly cheaper than mega-cap competitors trading in the mid-to-high 20s.

Note that Wall Street analysts currently have a consensus Buy rating on Meta Platforms Inc.

Managing downside risks ahead of macro volatility

Looking ahead, Dan Niles cautions against ignoring broader market technicals, drawing parallels to previous market "AI speed bumps" where overextended equities underwent rapid, sharp drawdowns within weeks.

Although enterprise execution at companies like Meta offers compelling individual upside, macroeconomic headwinds – ranging from aggressive sovereign borrowing to persistent inflation pressures – continue to increase systemic risk across stocks.

Investors navigating this environment must weigh strong fundamental catalysts against a tightening macroeconomic backdrop.

Rather than chasing market momentum, the seasoned market strategist suggests maintaining cash reserves and tactical hedges until seasonal corrections clear the path for more favorable risk-reward entry points.

data.title: Qualcomm stock rises 3.9% as AWS deal boosts data center outlook
data.description:
Qualcomm (QCOM) stock rose 3.9% in trading after StoneX reiterated a Buy rating and $270 price target, highlighting the chipmaker’s expanding data center ambitions and growing exposure to hyperscale customers.

The investment case comes as Qualcomm seeks to diversify beyond its core handset business, where demand remains uneven.

Analysts pointed to the company’s agreement with Amazon Web Services as a key development supporting its longer-term data center strategy.

AWS deal supports Qualcomm’s data center expansion

Qualcomm announced its collaboration with AWS on September 8, under which the chipmaker will supply custom silicon and advanced optical connectivity solutions.

The agreement could generate up to $60 billion in payments over multiple generations and the next decade.

The deal includes 25 million warrants issued to Amazon at an exercise price of $161.26.

Of those, 3.75 million shares are already vesting, while the remaining warrants depend on Amazon meeting payment milestones.

Unlike some recent AI chip agreements involving customer warrants, Amazon would have to pay $4 billion to acquire all of the shares.

Qualcomm’s stock would also need to remain above the $161 exercise price for Amazon to benefit from the warrants.

Qualcomm has set a target of $5 billion in data center revenue by fiscal 2027 and more than $15 billion by fiscal 2029.

The AWS agreement provides a publicly identified hyperscaler customer as the company works towards those targets.

At the Goldman Sachs Communacopia conference, Qualcomm’s CFO said the fiscal 2027 revenue target remains at $5 billion, with Amazon orders expected to begin in the December quarter.

Qualcomm targets growth beyond handsets

Stone Fox Capital said Qualcomm is executing a major pivot from handsets toward AI data centers, highlighting the AWS agreement as an important part of that strategy.

The firm noted Qualcomm’s $15 billion data center revenue target for fiscal 2029, while non-handset sales are projected to reach $40 billion.

It also said the AWS agreement could accelerate Qualcomm’s data center revenue ramp.

The Stone Fox Capital analyst added that the stock trades at roughly 10 times its fiscal 2029 earnings target of $18 per share, arguing that the market may not fully reflect the potential of Qualcomm’s AI-related growth.

The diversification push is also taking place as Qualcomm faces the loss of business from Apple.

Apple is increasingly shifting its iPhone modem operations toward internally developed technology, which could eventually cost Qualcomm around $4 billion to $5 billion in handset revenue, according to Counterpoint Research.

MediaTek adds near-term smartphone competition

Qualcomm’s data center expansion comes as competition remains active in its core smartphone market.

Rival MediaTek launched its Dimensity 9600 Pro, described in the supplied analysis as the first 2nm smartphone chip to market.

The launch comes one week before Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 launch, scheduled for September 22–24.

The development adds pressure in the premium smartphone segment as Qualcomm prepares its next-generation mobile processor.

The post Qualcomm stock rises 3.9% as AWS deal boosts data center outlook appeared first on Invezz

data.title: Why is Vera Therapeutics stock reversing its premarket gains?
data.description:
Vera Therapeutics (VERA) shares ripped higher in premarket trading on September 15 as investors reacted to landmark clinical data.

The biopharmaceutical firm announced that its lead therapy TRUTAKNA (atacicept-vymj) met all primary and secondary endpoints in the final 104-week efficacy analysis of its Phase 3 ORIGIN 3 trial for primary IgA nephropathy (IgAN).

VERA’s study demonstrated a notable 76% risk reduction in kidney disease progression alongside true kidney function stabilization.

Including today’s decline, Vera Therapeutics stock is down more than 30% versus its year-to-date high.

Why Vera Therapeutics stock rallied earlier today

Tuesday’s explosive premarket rally in VERA shares was ignited by outstanding top-line findings from the 428-patient ORIGIN 3 trial, evaluating TRUTAKNA in adults with progressive IgA nephropathy – a severe autoimmune kidney disease that frequently leads to kidney failure.

Patients receiving the weekly autoinjector achieved an annualized eGFR (kidney function) slope decline of just -0.6 mL/min/1.73m² over two years, compared to a steep -5.6 mL/min/1.73m² annual drop in the placebo cohort.

Plus, zero patients in the TRUTAKNA group required long-term dialysis, kidney transplantation, or died from kidney-related causes.

Building on its accelerated FDA approval granted earlier this summer, Vera confirmed plans to submit a supplemental Biologics License Application (sBLA) for full FDA approval in Q4 2026.

Why VERA shares pared back gains

Despite the stellar clinical outcomes, Vera Therapeutics shares quickly began giving up their early premarket gains as market hours approached.

Financial analysts point to a classic "sell the news" dynamic following a prolonged period of high market expectations.

Because TRUTAKNA had already secured accelerated FDA clearance in July and initial launch metrics were strong – with over 350 patient start forms generated in its first ten weeks – much of the ORIGIN 3 success was already priced into the stock's massive YTD run.

Additionally, valuation reality has stepped into focus: as a commercial-stage biotech scaling up operations, VERA reports zero prior product revenue and persistent net losses, alongside notable insider net selling ($8.3 million offloaded over the past 12 months), prompting short-term traders to lock in profits.

Should you buy Vera Therapeutics at the current price?

For long-term biotech investors, today’s intraday reversal presents a compelling structural entry point rather than a red flag.

Wall Street analysts remain decidedly bullish on Vera Therapeutics, maintaining a consensus "Buy" rating with an average 12-month price prediction of $77 – representing over 120% potential upside from its current trading range near $34.

The company boasts a robust balance sheet with a current liquidity ratio of nearly 10.9 and manageable debt, providing ample cash runway to support its commercial rollout.

While short-term trading may remain volatile as profit-taking settles, TRUTAKNA’s disease-modifying clinical profile positions Vera as a potential category leader in the multi-billion-dollar IgAN market ahead of its Q4 full FDA submission.

The post Why is Vera Therapeutics stock reversing its premarket gains? appeared first on Invezz

data.title: Apple stock falls as analysts assess iPhone 18 pro and foldable demand
data.description:
Apple Inc. (AAPL) stock traded about 1% lower on Tuesday as broader market sentiment remained cautious, despite relative strength in the technology sector.

The stock move comes as investors assess Apple’s latest iPhone cycle, the rollout of its redesigned Siri assistant, and analyst views on demand for the company’s new devices.

Apple rolls out redesigned Siri

Apple released iOS 27 on Monday, introducing its redesigned Siri AI assistant in beta just days before the company’s latest iPhones are scheduled to reach stores.

The update brings Apple’s delayed Siri overhaul back into focus as the company works to expand its consumer artificial intelligence offerings.

Users must opt in through the Settings app to access the new Siri, while some users may have to join a waitlist before gaining access, CNBC reported.

Apple first announced a more personalised, AI-powered Siri in 2024, but the upgraded assistant was delayed last year.

The rollout coincides with the company’s latest hardware cycle and could provide another reason for customers to upgrade their devices.

Analysts have also pointed to Apple’s large installed base and ageing iPhone fleet as potential support for a broader replacement cycle.

Analysts see growth potential from iPhone cycle

Deepwater Asset Management’s Gene Munster expects Apple’s staggered iPhone launch schedule to shift some growth into the March and June quarters.

Wall Street expects roughly 14% to 15% growth in the March quarter, according to Munster. He believes growth could approach 20% as delayed product launches contribute to sales.

Munster also highlighted Apple’s pricing power, noting that previous price increases had little effect on customer retention. That suggests consumers remain relatively loyal to the company’s ecosystem.

Yorkville Ives founding partner Dan Ives sees another potential catalyst in Apple’s installed base. He estimates that around 300 million iPhones have not been upgraded in more than four years, creating a sizeable replacement opportunity as Apple adds more AI capabilities.

Ives also expects a planned foldable iPhone, referred to as Duo, to eventually account for 15% to 20% of sales among Pro and Pro Max customers.

He expects limited customer churn from a roughly $100 price increase, although he cautioned that Apple’s pricing power has limits as higher memory costs pressure margins.

iPhone 18 lead times trail last year

Evercore ISI reiterated an Outperform rating and $365 price target on Apple following the start of pre-orders for the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max.

Pre-orders began on September 12, with the devices scheduled to launch on September 18.

Average delivery times for the Pro Max stood at 25 days, compared with 19 days last year, while the Pro showed 16 days versus 12 days previously.

However, JPMorgan said early delivery lead times for the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max were tracking below last year’s iPhone 17 launch.

The bank’s analysts, led by Samik Chatterjee, said global at-home delivery timing averaged seven days for the Pro and 19 days for the Pro Max, compared with 15 and 24 days, respectively, a year earlier.

The US, which accounts for about 34% of iPhone shipments, showed lead times of two days for the Pro and 22 days for the Pro Max, compared with four and 21 days last year.

China recorded the largest year-over-year shift, with lead times of 13 days for the Pro and 21 days for the Pro Max, compared with 30 days for both models last year.

JPMorgan expects the foldable Duo to gain traction in China, where consumers have already been exposed to foldable devices from domestic manufacturers.

JPMorgan cautioned against drawing firm conclusions from the early data, noting that supply allocations can differ from previous years.

The analysts said tracking how lead times change over time will be important for assessing underlying demand.
